gaps.note: No dimensioned drawing, 3D model or stencil of the faces is held. Both faces are measured off the maker's photographs and every position is estimated (provenance `method`).
gaps.wanted: A dimensioned front and rear view of the ACS800.

gaps.note: No photograph or picture of the four-port unit's rear is held. The rear is the two-port photograph and the data sheet's eight-port picture, and the four jacks are the first two gangs of the eight-port picture.
gaps.wanted: A photograph of the ACS804MEAC-400 rear.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 1.161 in and the installer guide, Table A.2, 1.3 in, a difference of 3.5 mm. Width and depth agree. The data sheet's figure is used.
gaps.wanted: The maker's height of the unit with and without its feet.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 2.4 lb and the installer guide, Table A.2, 3.8 lb (1.72365 kg), which is 1.72 kg only if the pound figure is rounded. No weight is stated.
gaps.wanted: The maker's weight for the ACS804MEAC-400.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives an external AC/DC adapter and a maximum of 28 W at 120 VAC and 240 VAC. The installer guide, Table A.2, gives an internal 100 to 240 VAC supply and 17 W maximum. The rear carries a 12VDC jack and the mounting guide tells the installer to place "the power supply" behind the unit, so the data sheet is used. The adapter is not drawn: no held document gives its size or its draw.
gaps.wanted: The maker's power figures for the ACS804MEAC-400 and the adapter's part number.

gaps.note: The four front USB ports are not numbered on the unit. The upper port of the first block is drawn as 1.
gaps.wanted: The maker's numbering of the USB ports.

gaps.note: The mounting guide shows optional DIN rail, wall and 1U shelf kits that bolt to the bottom edge of the unit. No figure dimensions a bracket or a hole and no kit part number is held, so no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: The kit part numbers and a dimensioned drawing of each kit.

gaps.note: Only the front and rear are photographed straight on. The top is seen at a slant in both photographs as a plain lid with a small mark at the rear corner and no vents; no photograph shows the bottom or a side.
gaps.wanted: Photographs or a drawing of the top, bottom and sides.

chassis.note: 8.374 x 7.156 x 1.161 in (W x D x H), data sheet AV-12340 page 2, converted to 212.7 x 181.76 x 29.49 mm. The installer guide, Table A.2, prints 1.3 x 8.38 x 7.16 in (H x W x D): the width and depth agree to 0.01 in and the height does not (gap `height`). The data sheet's figure is used because it is printed to a thousandth of an inch.

colour.note: medians of the front photograph: the face #494949 with an orange trim line along its bottom edge #ec8e30; of the rear photograph: the rear plate #edeef0 under a dark lid #515151. The lid is seen from above in both photographs and is not a face.

digital-out.note: Installer guide, "Digital Out sensors": "the four pins of the green connector form two switches", Switch 1 the two pins on the left and Switch 2 the two on the right, relays rated 12 A and 300 V. The guide's Table A.2 says "four output signals" and its text two digital outputs; both fit two switches of two pins. The front is the only face that carries it.

ears.note: Mounting Installation Guide 590-1509-501A: an optional kit of two brackets with DIN clips for 35 mm rail (page 1), an optional kit of two brackets for a wall (page 2) and an optional kit of two brackets and a 1U shelf (page 3). No kit is part of the unit, none is dimensioned and no kit part number is held, so the unit is a desktop box with no ears and no rack units.

front-layout.note: From the front photograph. The mark and the product name Avocent ACS800 sit at the left, the STATUS and POWER lamps follow, then four jacks in a row: MODEM, DIGITAL IN, the DIGITAL OUT connector and SENSOR, then two blocks of two stacked USB ports each, with the USB symbol under each block. The MODEM, DIGITAL IN and SENSOR jacks are RJ45 housings in white bezels, 20.6 mm apart centre to centre (MODEM to DIGITAL IN) and 41.3 mm (DIGITAL IN to SENSOR, the DIGITAL OUT connector between). The photograph does not number the USB ports; the upper port of the first block is taken as 1, the lower as 2, then the second block.

lamps.note: Installer guide Table 1.4, callout 1: the STATUS lamp is green when the console system is fully booted up and initialized and the Power lamp is green when power is being supplied. Table 1.5 gives each serial jack a green and a yellow lamp with the meanings written under each state.

method.note: NO DRAWING IS HELD, SO EVERY POSITION ON BOTH FACES IS MEASURED OFF THE MAKER'S PHOTOGRAPHS AND IS ESTIMATED. The front is the 800 x 600 front photograph: the face is 690 pixels across for the 212.7 mm body, 3.244 pixels per millimetre, and a jack's 52 pixel width reads 16.0 mm against the 15.8 mm of an RJ45 housing. The photograph looks slightly down on the unit, so every y is taken from the bottom edge of the face with the same scale. The rear is the data sheet's picture of the eight-port unit, rendered at 400 dpi (7.457 pixels per millimetre across the body), and the two-port rear photograph (3.40 pixels per millimetre) is the second reading: the first jack pair sits at 77.4 mm in the photograph and 77.6 mm in the picture, and the two jacks of the pair 14.4 mm apart in the photograph and 14.5 mm in the picture. A position is good to about 0.5 mm across and 1 mm down. Counts and colours are read directly.

power.note: Data sheet power usage: nominal 120 VAC typical 0.13 A and 6.2 W, maximum 0.47 A and 28 W; nominal 240 VAC typical 0.10 A and 7 W, maximum 0.29 A and 28 W. 28 W is the maximum at both and is filed as `power-max-w`. The supply is an external AC/DC adapter, 100 to 240 VAC in and 12 VDC out; the rear carries the 12VDC jack the adapter plugs into. The installer guide, Table A.2, gives an internal supply and 17 W maximum: gap `power`.

rear-layout.note: From the data sheet's eight-port rear picture and the two-port rear photograph. The 12VDC jack is at the left, then CONSOLE, then LAN 1 and LAN 2 with a green lamp at the upper left and a yellow at the upper right of each, then the serial jacks in gangs of two (a framed pair each) with a green lamp at the lower left and a yellow at the lower right of every jack. The eight-port picture shows gangs of 2, 2 and 4; the photograph shows the first pair. THE REAR OF THE FOUR-PORT UNIT IS NOT PHOTOGRAPHED: its four serial jacks are drawn as the first two gangs of the eight-port picture, at the positions that picture gives them, and the numbers 1 to 4 under them as printed on both pictures.

serial-ports.note: Data sheet hardware specifications: 2, 4 or 8 serial ports on RJ45, selectable between RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485, one serial console port on RJ45. Installer guide Table 1.4 callout 5: all of the serial ports are multi-protocol. The ordering table lists the 4-port unit only.

serial-role.note: Installer guide Table 1.4, callout 5: connect "the appropriate serial and power devices" to the serial ports. Callout 7 is the console port. The serial ports are console server ports as on the ACS8000.

sku.note: The data sheet ordering table lists one model, ACS804MEAC-400, "ACS800 4-port unit w/analog modem, external AC/DC, PDU cable". The data sheet says the family has 2, 4 or 8 serial ports and no held document gives the part number of the 2-port or the 8-port unit.

sources.note: Vertiv Avocent ACS800 Serial Console data sheet AV-12340 (R09/22): the ordering table, hardware specifications, power usage and dimensions, and its pictures of the front and of the eight-port rear. Vertiv Avocent ACS800/8000 Advanced Console System Installer/User Guide (PDF built 2025-03-05): Figure 1.4 and Table 1.4 (the callouts), Table 1.5 (the serial lamp states), "Digital Out sensors" (the two relay switches) and Table A.2. Avocent ACS800 Advanced Console System Mounting Installation Guide 590-1509-501A, pages 1 to 3: the DIN rail, wall and 1U shelf kits. The maker's product photographs of the front and of the two-port rear. No dimensioned drawing, 3D model or stencil is held.
